[[Persipura Jayapura|Persipura]] | prevseason = [[2020 Liga 1 (Indonesia)|2020]] | nextseason = [[2022–23 Liga 1 (Indonesia)|2022–23]] }} The '''2021–22 Liga 1''', also known as '''BRI Liga 1''' for sponsorship reasons,{{cite web |title=BRI Diperkenalkan sebagai Sponsor Utama Baru Liga 1 pada 12 Agustus 2021 |url=http://islamworldnews.com |website=bola.com |access-date=5 August 2021 |language=id |date=5 August 2021}} was the 5th season of [[Liga 1 (Indonesia)|Liga 1]] under its current name and the 12th season of the top-flight Indonesian professional league for [[association football]] clubs since its establishment in 2008. The season started on 27 August 2021.{{cite web |title=Liga 1 2021-2022 akan Digelar Mulai 20 Agustus |url=https://www.pssi.org/news/liga-1-2021-2022-akan-digelar-mulai-20-agustus |website=PSSI - Football Association of Indonesia |access-date=3 August 2021 |language=id-ID |archive-date=3 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803085135/https://www.pssi.org/news/liga-1-2021-2022-akan-digelar-mulai-20-agustus |url-status=dead }} [[Bali United F.C.|Bali United]] were the defending champions from the [[2019 Liga 1|2019 season]] after the [[2020 Liga 1 (Indonesia)|2020]] season was abandoned and declared void after three matches due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia|COVID-19 pandemic]]. On 25 March 2022, Bali United succeeded in defending their title for the second consecutive season, after second-placed [[Persib Bandung|Persib]] drew against [[Persik Kediri|Persik]], giving Bali United a 4-point lead with only one game left.{{cite news|url=https://bolanas.bolasport.com/read/493204577/kalah-telak-dari-persebaya-bali-united-tetap-back-to-back-juara-liga-1|title=Kalah Telak dari Persebaya, Bali United Tetap Back to Back Juara Liga 1|last=Nugroho|first=Nungki|date=25 March 2022|work=Bolanas.com|language=id}} == Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic == === Cancellation of the 2020 season === PSSI canceled the [[2020 Liga 1 (Indonesia)|2020 Liga 1]] season after putting it under suspension twice due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The first suspension was announced after finishing matchday three on 15 March 2020, two weeks after the government announced the first cases of [[COVID-19]] in Indonesia. The initial suspension was only for two weeks but it was extended to 29 May 2020. However, the government blocked every attempt to resume the competition.{{cite web |title=Kemenpora dan PSSI Hentikan Liga 1 dan Liga 2 karena Virus Corona |url=https://www.indosport.com/sepakbola/20200314/kemenpora-dan-pssi-hentikan-liga-1-dan-liga-2-karena-virus-corona |website=INDOSPORT.com |access-date=14 March 2020 |language=en |date=14 March 2020}} On 27 June 2020, [[Football Association of Indonesia|PSSI]] issued a decree to continue Liga 1 from October 2020.{{cite web |title=PSSI Keluarkan Surat Keputusan Lanjutkan Kembali Kompetisi Liga |url=https://www.pssi.org/news/pssi-keluarkan-surat-keputusan-lanjutkan-kembali-kompetisi-liga |website=PSSI - Football Association of Indonesia |access-date=28 June 2020 |language=id-ID |archive-date=28 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628212559/https://www.pssi.org/news/pssi-keluarkan-surat-keputusan-lanjutkan-kembali-kompetisi-liga |url-status=dead }} After failing to obtain government and police permissions for the umpteenth time, PSSI on 29 September 2020 announced the second postponement of the 2020 season of Liga 1 and Liga 2. This time the initial suspension had a one-month period. After the end date was reached, PSSI on 29 October 2020 declared the 2020 football seasons could not be held in 2020. There was an attempt to resume the 2020 season in 2021. However, on 15 January 2021, PSSI decided to cancel the 2020 season of all football competitions and declared them void.{{cite web |title=Resmi! PSSI Bubarkan Liga 1 2020 |url=https://bola.okezone.com/read/2021/01/20/51/2347835/resmi-pssi-bubarkan-liga-1-2020 |website=Okezone|access-date=20 January 2021 |language=id-ID}}{{cite web |title=Kompetisi Liga 1 dan 2 Batal Digelar Tahun Ini |url=https://republika.co.id/berita/qiyd9a438/kompetisi-liga-1-dan-2-batal-digelar-tahun-ini |website=Republika Online |access-date=29 October 2020 |language=id |date=29 October 2020}} === 2021 season plans === PSSI and PT LIB plan to hold the 2021 season in coordination with the [[Indonesian Police]] and other state agencies despite the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic in [[Indonesia]], the country with the most COVID-19 cases in [[Southeast Asia]]. The original plan was to hold it from 11 June 2021 and finish on 11 March 2022. After months of debate, PSSI decided against eliminating the relegation and promotion system, an option that many cash-strapped clubs proposed. PSSI also changed the starting date to early July 2021. COVID-19 restrictions in many cities on [[Java]] island delayed the commencement to late August 2021.{{cite web |title=Liga 1 Dijadwalkan Mulai 11 Juni 2021 - 11 Maret 2022, Format Kompetisi Penuh|url=https://www.bola.com/indonesia/read/4480959/liga-1-dijadwalkan-mulai-11-juni-2021-11-maret-2022-format-kompetisi-penuh |website=Bola.com |access-date=18 March 2021 |language=id |date=14 February 2021}}{{cite web |title=PSSI Putuskan Liga 1 dan Liga 2 Tetap Terapkan Sistem Degradasi|url=https://sport.detik.com/sepakbola/liga-indonesia/d-5583465/pssi-putuskan-liga-1-dan-liga-2-tetap-terapkan-sistem-degradasi|website=Detik.com |access-date=29 May 2021 |language=id |date=26 May 2021}} In order to obtain government permission, PSSI and PT LIB themselves had to incorporate various COVID-19 restrictions for the 2021 season, including disallowing fans to be inside or outside the stadium before, during, and after matches. Only a maximum of 299 people, including players, coaches, team officials, security personnel, and special guests, are allowed to enter the stadium. In addition, all entrants are required to be tested, pass temperature checks, wear masks, and follow other health protocols. All players also must be fully vaccinated to be eligible to play. All matches are expected to be played on main island of [[Java]] to reduce contagion risks from air travel, leading to protests from non-Java teams that must relocate their base to a Java city.{{cite web |title=Ketat, Begini Rencana PSSI Terkait Penerapan Protokol Kesehatan di Liga 1 2021|url=https://bola.okezone.com/read/2021/02/18/49/2364466/ketat-begini-rencana-pssi-terkait-penerapan-protokol-kesehatan-di-liga-1-2021|website=Okezone |access-date=18 February 2021 |language=id |date=18 March 2021}}{{cite web |title=Ketua PSSI Pastikan Liga 1 Digelar Terpusat di Pulau Jawa Mulai Juli 2021|url=https://sport.tempo.co/read/1465448/ketua-pssi-pastikan-liga-1-digelar-terpusat-di-pulau-jawa-mulai-juli-2021|website=Tempo.co|access-date=29 May 2021 |language=id|date=24 May 2021}} As a simulation for the 2021 season, PSSI held the [[2021 Menpora Cup]] as a pre-season tournament for the Liga 1 teams. The event was held as a reference in implementing health protocols so that government and police officials become convinced that professional football matches would not turn into super-spreader events.{{cite web |title=Apa & Kapan Piala Menpora 2021 - Jadwal, Hasil & Info Lengkap Turnamen Pramusim Perdana Era Covid-19|url=https://www.goal.com/id/berita/apa-kapan-piala-menpora-2021-jadwal-hasil-info-lengkap/1w5dgltusqhhn1gyma5anss917|website=Goal Indonesia |access-date=15 March 2021 |language=id |date=18 March 2021}} === 2021 format=== Cognizant of the fluctuating situation caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, PSSI and PT LIB decided the league format will be divided into six series that consider the infection levels across Java island. Each series will cover 45-54 matches (five to six matchdays) played in multiple designated regions to ensure no club will play in their home grounds. The venues can change days ahead of schedule if certain regions are deemed as COVID-19 red zones or violations to COVID-19 rules occurred at a specific stadium.{{cite web |title=Liga 1 Tetap Gunakan Sistem Enam Series|url=https://www.jawapos.com/sepak-bola/sepak-bola-indonesia/05/08/2021/liga-1-tetap-gunakan-sistem-enam-series-dan-tiga-klaster/|website=JawaPos.com |access-date=5 September 2021 |language=id |date=5 August 2021}} The first series (six matchdays) will be held in the provinces of [[Banten]], [[West Java]], and [[DKI Jakarta]] with six stadiums ([[Benteng Taruna Stadium]], [[Pakansari Stadium]], [[Patriot Stadium (Indonesia)]], [[Wibawa Mukti Stadium]], [[Gelora Bandung Lautan Api Stadium]] and [[Jalak Harupat Stadium]]). The second series is planned to be held in the provinces [[Central Java]] and [[Special Region of Yogyakarta]] with five stadiums ([[Jatidiri Stadium]], Citarum Stadium, [[Manahan Stadium]], [[Maguwoharjo Stadium]] and [[Sultan Agung Stadium]]). The third series is planned to entirely run in [[East Java]] province but in different nine stadiums ([[Gelora Bung Tomo Stadium]], [[Gelora 10 November Stadium]], [[Kanjuruhan Stadium]], [[Gajayana Stadium]], [[Surajaya Stadium]], [[Petrokimia Stadium]], [[Gelora Delta Stadium]], [[Brawijaya Stadium]], [[Gelora Bangkalan Stadium]]).{{cite web |title=24 Stadion di Seluruh Pulau Jawa Bakal Jadi Venue Liga 1 |url=https://www.bola.com/indonesia/read/4570841/24-stadion-di-seluruh-pulau-jawa-bakal-jadi-venue-liga-1-2021-2022-mulai-sugbk-hingga-manahan|website=Bola.com |access-date=5 September 2021 |language=id |date=1 June 2021}} The fourth and fifth series will be held in [[Bali]] with limited supporters in four stadiums ([[Kapten I Wayan Dipta Stadium]] (Gianyar), [[Ngurah Rai Stadium]] (Denpasar), [[Kompyang Sujana Stadium]] (Denpasar), and [[Samudra Stadium]] (Badung)), before the sixth and last series is planned to take place at venues in the kick-off series in the provinces of [[Banten]], [[West Java]], and [[DKI Jakarta]].{{cite web |title=Seri 4 & 5 Liga 1 2021 Bakal Berlangsung di Bali dan Hadirkan Penonton
